## What is the Command Line

- A way to control the computer by typing instead of clicking
- You type a command and press **Enter**
- The computer runs the command and prints the result
- Programmers use it every day

## The Terminal and the Shell

- The **terminal** is the window where you type
- The **shell** is the program inside it that reads your commands
- The shell runs each command and shows you the output
- The terminal is the screen, the shell is the one listening

## What is Bash

- **Bash** is one of the most common shells
- It is the default on Linux and in GitHub Codespaces
- It is also available on macOS and Windows
- The commands in this lesson work the same in all of them

## The Prompt

```
#
```

- The `#` is the **prompt** - the shell is waiting for a command
- Type the command after the prompt
- Press **Enter** to run it
- The output appears on the lines below

## Our Example: Files and Folders

```
/Users/calvinw
├── notes.txt
├── todo.txt
└── projects
    ├── index.html
    ├── about.html
    └── style.css
```

- `/Users/calvinw` is our starting folder
- It holds two files and one directory
- The directory `projects` has three files inside it

## pwd - Where Am I

- `pwd` stands for **print working directory**
- It prints the folder the shell is currently in
- Every command runs relative to this folder

```
# pwd
/Users/calvinw
```

## ls - What Is Here

- `ls` **lists** the files and directories in the current folder
- It does not change anything, it only shows what is there

```
# ls
notes.txt  projects  todo.txt
```

- Two files and the `projects` directory

## cd - Change Directory

- `cd` **changes directory** - it moves the shell into another folder
- Type `cd` followed by the name of the folder
- It prints nothing when it works

```
# cd projects
#
```

## Check That cd Worked

- Run `pwd` again to see the new working directory

```
# pwd
/Users/calvinw/projects
```

- The shell is now inside `projects`

## ls Inside the Directory

- Run `ls` again - the shell is in a different folder now
- It lists the files in `projects`

```
# ls
about.html  index.html  style.css
```

## Putting It Together

```
# pwd
/Users/calvinw
# ls
notes.txt  projects  todo.txt
# cd projects
# pwd
/Users/calvinw/projects
# ls
about.html  index.html  style.css
```

## Summary

| Command | Meaning | What it does |
|---------|---------|--------------|
| `pwd` | print working directory | Shows where you are |
| `ls` | list | Shows the files here |
| `cd` | change directory | Moves you into a folder |
